extraction.segment_function: Discusses Hannah Arendt's metaphorics of indoor and outdoor spaces, her relation to Athenian civic ideology, and her reading of Plato's allegory of the cave in the Republic.

claims.claim: Arendt's concepts are connected loosely and connotatively to outdoor and indoor spaces and their associations with exposure and shelter.
claims.supporting_excerpt: her concepts seem only loosely and connotatively connected to outdoor and indoor spaces, and to their association of these spaces with exposure and shelter respectively .
qualifications: Even in passages that do not make reference to Greece

claims.claim: Arendt read Plato's cave allegory as a celebratory account of the philosopher's flight from the dark cave of human affairs into the bright sky of ideas.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Arendt read this allegory , ﬂatly , as Plato ’s celebratory account of the philosopher ’s ﬂight from the “dark cave of human affairs, ” where everything is mere appearance, into the “bright sky of ideas ” where the “true essence of Being ” can be seen

must_not_be_lost: Arendt's understanding of publicity and privacy did not simply reproduce Athenian civic ideology.
Plato initiated a tradition that recast the polis as a locus of necessity to be ruled by the philosopher as a despot rules the household.
